film.title: Pass No. 26: Ed Delahanty, the Best Hitter of His Century, and the Bridge at Niagara
film.description:
July 2, 1903. Ed Delahanty, the best hitter of the century that had just ended, is put off a Michigan Central sleeper at Bridgeburg, Ontario. He walks out onto the International Bridge in the dark, over the Niagara River. A week later his body is found below the Falls. They knew who had gone off the bridge by what was in his valise: a season pass to the Washington ballpark, No. 26.

This film tells it from the newspapers of that week: the conductor, the night watchman, the open draw, the valise, and the money fight between the leagues that sent Del back to Washington owing a bill. Delahanty was born in Cleveland in 1867, hit .346 for his career, and went into the Hall of Fame in 1945. His stone in Cleveland's Calvary Cemetery carries one word.

A Hardwood Bricks Productions film, in association with JuiceboxNationTV Entertainment. A JuiceBall presentation. A 19 North Films film. Written by Matthew Hagan.

How this was made: the narrator is an AI clone of Matthew's voice. The 1903 newspaper lines are read by AI voices. The train, ballpark and riverside scenes are AI reenactments and are labeled on screen. The pass and the stone are illustrations. Music is original. Niagara photographs and Whirlpool footage by Hardwood Bricks.

Sources: The Evening World (New York), July 8, 1903; The Salt Lake Herald, July 9 and 10, 1903; The Courier-Journal (Louisville), July 10 and 13, 1903; Bisbee Daily Review, July 10, 1903; The St. Louis Republic, July 12, 1903; The Washington Times, Oct. 14, 1903; Waterbury Evening Democrat, July 6, 1903; Daily Kennebec Journal, July 9, 1903. Newspapers, photographs and Edison films from the Library of Congress, Chronicling America. Career record: Society for American Baseball Research; National Baseball Hall of Fame.

Photo credits: Babe Ruth, Bain News Service, Library of Congress. Barry Bonds, photo by Jim Accordino, CC BY. Shohei Ohtani, photo by All-Pro Reels, CC BY-SA 2.0 (cropped).

reels.title: The best hitter of his century, on a bridge in the dark
reels.text: July 2, 1903. Ed Delahanty has had five whiskeys and is holding an open razor on a sleeper bound for Buffalo. In about an hour he is on a bridge over the Niagara River.

reels.title: How they knew who went off the bridge: Pass No. 26
reels.text: Not a face. A tailor's label, and a free pass to his own ballpark, left in a valise on the train. Ed Delahanty, Niagara, 1903.
